_README: Rulings a human judged unpublishable, and why. This file is the only way to make a
removal stick: propose.py derives 'already handled' from the TSV's source column, so
deleting a row without recording it here means the next refresh re-proposes the same
comment, forever. applied_comment_ids() unions these comment ids in.
It is also the corpus's error log. Every entry is a case where the pipeline published
something wrong, kept in full so a later reviewer -- human or model -- can see the
failure mode rather than rediscover it. propose.py and curate.py are fed the reasons
as prompt context, so an entry here teaches the next run what not to do again.
misreads-source  the ruling does not say what its cited comment says (transcription bug)
not-official     the cited author is not a publisher/designer voice
hedged           the official answer was not firm ("could go either way", never followed up)
superseded       a later official answer contradicts it and is correct
duplicate        the card already carries this ruling, so publishing it adds only noise
wrong            substantively wrong for a reason other than the above
Never delete an entry to 'clean up'. Removing one un-blocks the comment and the ruling
returns. Only remove one if the rejection itself turns out to be the mistake.

reason: Brendan Dunne asked whether a [card] drawn with Wilson's Storm Petrel could be tucked
with Common Grackle instead of discarded. Jamey Stegmaier said yes -- but opened with
"I'll look up those birds to see what they do", quoted only the card text back, and
answered the wrong half of the question (whether you must discard) without addressing
whether the drawn cards are in your hand at all.
He corrected himself nine months later in comment 64737, quoting the Appendix: "These
cards should be kept separate from the other cards you draw and your bird cards in
hand. They cannot be spent during this turn." Joe Aubrey confirmed it again in 85569
("as confirmed by the appendix entries for those"). Cards that cannot be spent during
the turn cannot be tucked with Common Grackle, whose power tucks from your hand -- so
the published answer was the reverse of the rule.
Replaced on all three cards by rows citing 64737, which state the Appendix rule
directly and answer the tucking question that prompted the thread.
Failure mode to watch for: an official reply that visibly reasons from the card text
in the moment ("let me look that up", "I'm pretty sure", "I believe") is weaker
evidence than the same author citing the Appendix later. Improvisation markers in the
source are a signal to keep looking, not a reason to publish faster.
The published ruling asserted the exact opposite of its source. Eric Chow asked "So
the bird power activation is considered part of the main action. here 'gain food'
action?" and Jamey Stegmaier answered "A bird power about gaining food is not part of
the main action. The main actions are printed on the player mat." -- a no. The ruling
we published from it said Loggerhead Shrike triggers "including [rodent] gained from a
bird power activated during that action", i.e. a yes.
The transcription inverted the conclusion while copying the principle correctly, so the
text read as coherent and self-justifying, and curate.py then reasoned about it as the
newest ruling 'reversing' the four older ones -- a conflict that exists nowhere in the
source corpus. All five Stonemaier answers on this card agree: 20190405 (Jamey),
20191029 (Joe Aubrey), 20191218 (Jamey), 20260708 (Joe Aubrey, and the newest of all)
all say bird-power food does not trigger the Shrike.
Failure mode to watch for: a terse answer that negates the *premise* of a paraphrase
question ("So X counts as Y?" / "X is not Y"). The polarity lives in the question,
which is not quoted in the ruling, so nothing in the published text looks wrong.
Red Kite played on Long-Tailed Tit: both cards already carry the answer.
Long-Tailed Tit says "If a bird (e.g., Common Buzzard) is played on top of this one, the
top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns", and Red Kite says the
converse. The proposal adds only that the second space is not freed up, which is what
"occupies both columns" already means.
The covering-bird-also-goes-sideways rule is already published on all four cards.
Note this is the same rule as the newly added 20200218 rows on Grey Heron and Red Kite --
those were added because comment 36691 answers what happens to the *covered* bird (it
becomes a tucked card), which no existing row stated. This proposal restates only the
sideways placement.
Montagu's Harrier already carries "Even when using this bird's power to play it on top of
another bird, this bird may only be played in [grassland]." The proposal adds the reason
(it is a WHEN PLAYED power) but not the ruling.
Red-Bellied Woodpecker already carries "Because caching is optional, you may instead add
the [seed] gained with Red-Bellied Woodpecker's power to your personal food supply."
The proposal's "single action with a choice" framing is the same rule.
The duplicate detector's own note on this one is unreliable -- it cited Greylag Goose and
American Redstart, neither of which is related. Verified against master.json instead.
Cartographer already carries the closed-list rule ("The only keywords that qualify a bird
to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon..."), and Turkey Vulture already
carries the specific answer that "turkey" is not a geography term. Both halves published.
Photographer already carries the closed-list rule and, explicitly, "Substrings of bird
names that coincide with color names do not count toward this bonus when not referring to
colors" -- which is the Western Tanager / "tan" case verbatim.
Green Heron already carries "When another player uses Green Heron's power to trade a food
token for [nectar], that counts as gaining [nectar], so Spangled Drongo's power triggers."
That is the gain case in full, on the card players will be looking at.
The duplicate detector called this "genuinely new" because it compared against the
"trading counts as spending" row only; the gain case was on a different row of the same
card. A dup verdict that says "the existing ruling covers X, this is the complementary Y"
is worth checking against every row on the card, not just the one quoted.
Southern Cassowary already carries "When using this bird's power to discard another bird
from your mat, all food cached on that bird, [egg] laid on that bird, and [card] tucked
under that bird are discarded." The proposal is a narrower restatement of the same rule.
Turkey Vulture already carries the general ruling "You may activate each 'once between
turns' power on a bird on your player mat once between each of your turns." Two successful
predators in one opponent turn is exactly the case that rule decides.
Both Olive-Backed Sunbird and White-Browed Tit-Warbler already carry the general ruling
"You may only reroll dice when gaining food from the birdfeeder and not when gaining food
from the supply", which answers the question these powers raise. The Asia rulebook's
"from the birdfeeder" wording is a clarification of that same rule, not a new one.
Duplicate of rulings already on all three cards -- and where it differs, it is the weaker
answer. Coal Tit, Superb Lyrebird and Tui all state that a bird copying Coal Tit's power
"retains the ability to spend [seed] cached on it until the end of the turn but no longer".
Jamey Stegmaier's answer here instead ends the ability "after you're done activating the
Tui's power", which is narrower and uncorroborated.
Publishing it would put two different cut-off points on the same card. Per the
source-strength rule in domain-knowledge.md, a single forum reply does not displace a
ruling that the corpus already states three times consistently.
Jamey Stegmaier's answer is a double negative -- "no, it isn't missing the predator icon"
-- to a question about whether Little Owl's card is missing one. In context it almost
certainly means the card is correct as printed, but 'almost certainly' is not a standard
for a rules reference players use to settle arguments. The proposing model flagged it
itself and asked a reviewer to confirm before publishing, which is the right call.
Not blocked forever: if a firmer official answer turns up, remove this entry.
The published row said 2 [egg] on Eurasian Green Woodpecker count as 4 toward an
egg-counting end-of-round goal. The European Expansion rulebook says the opposite, in the
OTHER POWERS section: eggs on these cards are not doubled if the goal is counting eggs.
The rulebook line is quoted verbatim in comment 37614, the question Joe Aubrey answered.
Four official answers agree with the rulebook: 37617, 37745 and 43812 (Joe Aubrey) all
distinguish goals that count *birds* from goals that count eggs, food or columns. In 42749
Jamey Stegmaier withdrew his own contrary answer (42746) and deferred to BGG thread
2365136 -- which is the source of the ruling this row contradicted. Comment 116934 is
Jamey in 2025 repeating the error he had retracted in 2020, to a question that quoted the
card's power text but not the rulebook line.
Replaced by 20200401, 20200405b, 20210123 and 20220914, which state which goal types
double and which do not, per card.
Failure mode to watch for: recency is not the tie-breaker. A rulebook line, or a forum
answer that quotes one, outranks a later flat forum answer that does not -- especially
when the same author has already retracted that answer once.
Whether hummingbird cards count for Bird Bander. Bird Bander already carries a firmer,
broader ruling from a 2026 comment: hummingbirds count toward bonus cards in the ordinary
way, naming Bird Bander first. This adds nothing but a weaker version of it -- Jamey said
he 'could see it going either way' and only leaned toward counting them.
Two independent benefits in a power may be resolved in either order. Galah, the only card
named, already says exactly this ('The two clauses of Galah's power are independent'), from
a 2024 comment. The other half of the answer -- that an arrow means resolve left to right,
cost then benefit -- has no home: no card in the collection prints an arrow in its power
text (checked all 707), so the marker never reaches a player through wingsearch.
What an 'action cube' is, asked of Dunnock. The official comment confirms only the
definition of the game's own component -- the cube you place when you take a turn -- and
the rest of the proposed text ('count the cubes currently on the chosen player's grassland
row') is Dunnock's printed power restated. A glossary entry for a word the rulebook
defines is not a ruling.
Pink powers cannot trigger on their owner's turn. That is already published twice as a
general ruling, on all 51 pink birds ('You may not use a pink power during your turn' and
'You may use a pink power during another player's turn'), and European Goldfinch carries a
named ruling on its own once-between-turns timing. The remaining sentence -- that your own
pink power tucking during an opponent's turn does not re-trigger your own pink power but
can trigger theirs -- is the model's inference; the official answer does not address it.
Rejected together with comment 44865, which is the same question and the same answer.
Wedge-Tailed Eagle looks for wingspans *over* 65cm. That is the card's printed text; the
thread's actual official content was about the two Oceania cockatoos, whose cards were not
in the candidate list, and the rest is balance opinion. Nothing to publish.
A counts-double bird does not double a filled column. Cetti's Warbler and Eurasian Green
Woodpecker -- the two cards named -- already carry that sentence verbatim, sourced to
comment 54914, along with two more rulings on the same principle for other goal types.
Comment 42749 is a *retraction*: Jamey first said 'it counts in both columns', then
withdrew it. The withdrawal is worth nothing on its own once the correct answer is
already published.
Same question and same official answer as comment 38049 above (pink powers only on other
players' turns), already general on all 51 pink birds. See that entry.
The full-row bonus on the player mat may be used only once per turn. The answer is firm
and Jamey's, but it is a rule about the player mat, and this pipeline can only put text on
cards: general_map's predicates iterate the bird list, so a rule that belongs to no bird
reaches no page. Publishing it would mean inventing a card to hang it on.
Not a judgement on the ruling -- if wingsearch ever gains a rules-reference page outside
the card collection, this and comment 59885 belong on it.
Whether [seed] cached on Coal Tit can pay for Eurasian Nutcracker's 'from your supply'.
Jamey answered 'I would say it isn't in your supply, as your supply is off your mat' -- a
lean, not a ruling, and it cuts against Coal Tit's printed 'At any time, you may spend
[seed] cached on this card'.
It is also already settled better. Coal Tit carries a 2025 ruling drawing the exact line:
cached food counts as being in your supply *for the purpose of spending it*, but does not
satisfy powers that check what food is in your supply. Under that, paying the Nutcracker's
cost is spending, so the cached seed works -- the opposite of this lean. Publishing both
would leave two official-looking answers contradicting each other on the same card, which
is the failure mode wingsearch exists to avoid.
Multi-player choices go in turn order, clockwise from the current player. Jamey hedged
('I think it's a global rule in Wingspan'), and comment 159055 (2026) states the same rule
without hedging and adds what happens next -- the active player carries on with the
remaining brown powers. That one is now published as a general ruling on 69 birds,
including both cards named here.
Duet tokens are unaffected when Spotted Dove moves to another player's mat. Spotted Dove
already carries that ruling, sourced to comment 59660, and it is the better version: it
also says a duet token *is* placed if a bird is later played on the vacated space. Jamey
answered this one before seeing the card text.
The Asia printing of Anatomist awards 6 points instead of 7. Anatomist already carries
that, sourced to comment 58045, and names the tier the change applies to (4+ birds), which
this comment does not.
Great Cormorant's first sentence is skipped with no [fish] cached. Already published on
that card from comment 62565. The Red-Wattled Lapwing half of the answer restates the
card's printed text.
With 1 [die] left you may reroll for free, so paying [nectar] to reset the birdfeeder is
not allowed. Firm and Jamey's, but it is about the Oceania player mat's reset bonus rather
than any bird, so it has no card to attach to -- same problem as comment 45802. The free
reroll it depends on is published: comment 71887's statement of the reroll rules is now
general on 63 birdfeeder birds.
When a pink power triggers off a push-your-luck predator: after the whole hunt, or after
each successful roll. Jamey answered 'after the whole thing' in comment 65180, but in
comment 109154 -- later in the same thread -- he said the Appendix wording is open to
interpretation and that he would check with his team. No follow-up ever appeared.
An answer the designer himself reopened is the clearest possible case for not publishing.
Turkey Vulture also already carries the general timing rule: a pink power activates
directly after the triggering action, once the triggering player has finished all the
actions on the card that caused it.
That the Asia appendix is wrong about Verditer Flycatcher -- that the [invertebrate] must
be gained *before* the bird is activated, not before or after.
Jamey confirmed only the turn-order premise (core benefit first, then brown powers right
to left). The conclusion that the printed appendix clarification is therefore incorrect is
the model's inference, and printed rulebook text outranks a forum restatement of a premise
the printed text was written in full knowledge of. Publishing 'the appendix is wrong' on
an inference is exactly the kind of claim that costs a rules reference its credibility.
That a repeated Eurasian Nuthatch caches its [seed] on the repeating bird (Northern
Mockingbird) where it cannot later be spent. Jamey answered this in 2023, and it was
published on both cards; both rows are removed by this batch.
Two official answers say the opposite, and they bracket it in time. Joe Aubrey, comment
36250 (2020): the repeating bird 'does not take on the other bird's power; the other bird
repeats its own power as if it were activated again', so tucks go behind that bird and its
costs are paid as its own text specifies. Jamey, comment 150843 (2026), correcting himself
in the same thread after a player raised the distinction: a repeat makes the other bird's
power trigger again on that bird itself, and is not a copy performed by the repeating bird.
Jamey has erred on this exact distinction three times and corrected himself twice (see
comments 35726 and 150562/150650), so a lone Jamey comment on repeat-versus-copy is weak
evidence. Both of the answers above are now published on Gray Catbird and Northern
Mockingbird. Eurasian Nuthatch keeps its ruling that [seed] cached on it by another bird's
power can later be spent with its own power, which agrees with them.
